summary: Bezalel makes the gold-covered ark and its gold cover with cherubim, followed by the table and its vessels. The report then describes the one-piece branching lamp stand, the smaller incense altar, and the preparation of holy anointing oil and incense.
whyItMatters: The sanctuary’s principal furnishings move from earlier instructions into a report of completed work. Distinct techniques and carrying arrangements show how skilled work gives each object its particular form within a movable place of worship.

context.author: Exodus does not name its final author. It records Moses writing particular covenant material; traditional Mosaic attribution and modern accounts of composition are distinguished in the book briefing.
context.audience: Israel remembering its rescue from Egypt and its obligations as a covenant community. The chapter does not identify an individual dedicatee.
context.date: The narrative places these events at Sinai after the departure from Egypt. The date of the events and the history of the book’s composition are separate, debated questions.
context.setting: The sanctuary workshop in the Israelite camp during the construction following covenant renewal.
context.literaryForm: A craft-by-craft completion report moving through wooden furnishings, hammered gold work, and perfumery.

before.text: The enclosure's curtains, frame, veil, and doorway screen have been made. The narrative now turns to the objects that will stand within it.

here.text: The chapter groups the ark, table, lamp stand, incense altar, and mixtures while repeatedly distinguishing gold-covered wood from work made of pure gold.

after.text: The next report moves to the bronze altar, basin, and court, then accounts for the gold, silver, and bronze used in the work.

outline.heading: The ark and carrying apparatus
outline.note: Bezalel makes the wooden chest, gold covering, rings, and poles.

outline.heading: The cover and cherubim
outline.note: The gold figures and cover are made as one piece, with wings and faces oriented inward.

outline.heading: The table and vessels
outline.note: The gold-covered table receives its border, carrying equipment, and pure-gold vessels.

outline.heading: The one-piece lamp stand
outline.note: Branches, almond-flower forms, seven lamps, and accessories are made from gold.

outline.heading: The incense altar and sacred mixtures
outline.note: A small gold-covered altar is finished along with oil and incense made by the perfumer’s art.

keyVerses.text: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
keyVerses.why: The report begins with a named maker carrying out the ark’s specified construction.

keyVerses.text: Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole thing was one beaten work of pure gold.
keyVerses.why: The lamp stand’s connected parts are described as one beaten work of gold.

keyVerses.text: He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, after the art of the perfumer.
keyVerses.why: The final line includes specialist preparation of scent alongside wood and metal crafts.

questions.question: Why does the report begin with Bezalel’s name?
questions.answer: It identifies the maker at the start of the ark's construction and then follows the completed objects through repeated action statements. The account gives responsibility a named human setting even while the wider project is attributed to divine instruction.

questions.question: How does the ark’s cover relate to the chest?
questions.answer: The pure-gold cover has the same stated length and width as the wooden ark. The two cherubim are worked as one piece with the cover, with their faces and wings directed over it.

questions.question: What is meant by “beaten work”?
questions.answer: It describes gold shaped through hammering in the making of the cherubim and lamp stand. The report emphasizes the lamp stand's continuous construction: base, shaft, cups, buds, flowers, and branches belong to one work.

questions.question: What makes the table suitable for travel?
questions.answer: Gold rings are placed near the border at its four feet, and gold-covered acacia poles are fitted to carry it. Its portability is built into the object alongside the vessels used with it.

questions.question: Are the lamp stand’s six branches inconsistent with seven lamps?
questions.answer: No. Six branches extend from the sides of the central shaft, and the completed object receives seven lamps. The center and side branches together account for the seven-lamp arrangement.

questions.question: Does the chapter itself assign a spiritual meaning to every flower and material?
questions.answer: It carefully describes almond blossoms, buds, pure gold, and gold-covered wood as features of the completed objects. The report explains construction and form; it supplies no symbolic explanation for every detail, leaving such readings as additional interpretation.

questions.question: Why include oil and incense after the furniture?
questions.answer: The sanctuary's service requires prepared substances as well as permanent objects. The final verse credits the art of the perfumer, extending the account of skilled work beyond carpentry, engraving, and metal shaping.

glossary.def: The pure-gold cover made with cherubim for the top of the ark.
The flower forms reproduced in the cups decorating the lamp stand.
The craftsperson’s expertise invoked for compounding the holy oil and incense.
